details:
**"Funding secured" and taking Tesla private at $420**
In August 2018, Musk tweeted that he was "considering taking Tesla private at $420" per share and had "funding secured." The SEC sued him for securities fraud because the funding had not actually been arranged; he settled by paying a $20 million fine and stepping down as Tesla's chairman.

**SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Dragon**
SpaceX, the rocket company Musk founded in 2002, builds the reusable Falcon 9 rocket and the Dragon capsule. In May 2020, Crew Dragon's Demo-2 mission, commanded by NASA astronaut Doug Hurley alongside Bob Behnken, became the first crewed orbital launch by a private company.

**Tesla Roadster launched on Falcon Heavy**
For the first test flight of SpaceX's Falcon Heavy rocket in February 2018, Musk sent his own cherry-red Tesla Roadster into orbit around the Sun as a dummy payload. A spacesuit-clad mannequin named "Starman" sat in the driver's seat.

**$44 billion purchase of Twitter**
In 2022, Musk agreed to buy Twitter for about $44 billion. He tried to back out of the deal in July 2022, Twitter sued to force the sale, and he completed the purchase in October 2022, later renaming the platform X.

**Tesla gigafactories and car models**
Tesla is the electric-car company Musk leads as CEO, whose huge battery and car plants are called "gigafactories." Its vehicles include the original Roadster, the Model S sedan, the Model X SUV, the cheaper Model 3, and the angular stainless-steel Cybertruck.

**The Boring Company**
A tunnel-digging company Musk founded in 2016 to ease traffic congestion by building underground transportation tunnels, with early projects proposed in Los Angeles. Its name is a pun on boring, the process of drilling tunnels.

**"RIP Harambe"**
A heavily auto-tuned rap song Musk released on SoundCloud in 2019 as a tribute to Harambe, the gorilla shot at the Cincinnati Zoo in 2016 after a child fell into his enclosure.

**Fremont factory reopening during COVID-19**
In May 2020, Musk reopened Tesla's car factory in Fremont, California, in defiance of Alameda County's coronavirus lockdown orders. He sued the county and dared officials to arrest him, and the county later allowed the plant to reopen.

**"Tesla stock price is too high imo"**
A May 2020 tweet by Musk that caused Tesla's stock to drop sharply, wiping out billions of dollars in market value. When Tesla's share price later surged past $1,000, he responded by tweeting "lol."

**Hyperloop**
A proposed high-speed transportation system in which passenger pods would travel through low-pressure tubes at near-airliner speeds. Musk outlined the concept in a 2013 white paper, and other companies have since tried to develop it.

**"We will coup whoever we want!"**
A July 2020 tweet in which Musk replied to a user accusing the U.S. government of organizing the 2019 ouster of Bolivian president Evo Morales so Musk could obtain Bolivia's lithium, a key battery material. He added "Deal with it," and later deleted the tweet.

**"Space Karen"**
An insult aimed at Musk on Twitter in November 2020 after he complained about getting conflicting COVID-19 test results (two positive and two negative) on the same day. He had also downplayed the dangers of the pandemic.

**Richest South African**
Musk was born in Pretoria, South Africa, in 1971 and later moved to Canada and the United States. Thanks largely to his stakes in Tesla and SpaceX, he became the richest person in the world.
